name: PTR Reverse Lookup
description: Turn an IP address into its host name and check that forward and reverse records agree.

hints.query: Give an IP address to reverse it directly; with only a domain the first forward address is resolved first.
hints.output: The host names found by the reverse lookup are resolved forward again, so mismatches between forward and reverse records become visible.

faq.q: Is an empty reverse lookup normal?
faq.a: Yes. Many cloud hosts and containers ship without PTR records, especially when the security group forbids arbitrary reverse lookups.

faq.q: Why do the forward addresses and the reverse result disagree?
faq.a: The PTR record is out of sync: forward resolution uses the A or AAAA records while the reverse lookup uses the in-addr.arpa record of the IP.
Yes. IPv6 uses the ip6.arpa form of reverse names and follows the same resolution logic.
